subject.title: Feature Request: Add .gitignore-like exclude patterns to backup CLI

question: Should OpenClaw's native backup CLI add gitignore-style exclusions now, and what default/protected-path rules are acceptable for restore-critical and sensitive data?
rationale: This changes a core recovery and security command; the active PR shows unresolved choices around smart defaults, protected paths, auto-loaded ignore files, manifest contents, external assets, and proof that automation should not decide for maintainers.

options.title: Narrow and review the native PR
options.body: Keep this issue open and ask maintainers to narrow https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/44288 into an opt-in, proof-backed design with explicit protected restore paths and no silent backup-scope changes.

options.title: Defer native excludes
options.body: Keep the issue open as a product backlog item and direct users to Keep My Claw or manual cleanup until maintainers are ready to own the native CLI surface.

options.title: Reject native scope
options.body: Decide fine-grained filtering belongs outside core and close only after documenting the supported plugin or ClawHub alternative and its security tradeoffs.

recommendation.title: Narrow and review the native PR
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open and ask maintainers to narrow https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/44288 into an opt-in, proof-backed design with explicit protected restore paths and no silent backup-scope changes.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent current-main/release-line ownership makes this the best available routing candidate for the product/security decision, with original backup authors as supporting context.
